purpose: Build a realistic local securitized-product trade capture mock while measuring frontier planning and review, bounded mid-level and open-model implementation, integration repair, elapsed time, token telemetry, and metered cost.

baseline.resolution: Planning used the preregistered clean commit. Terra used B1. The remaining implementation workers use the same clean descendant containing B2, their frozen tasks, and the post-Terra harness repair.

workflow.task: created only after the saved Sol plan is committed

workflow.ownership: domain types, calculations, validation, seed data, and domain tests
application state, blotter, selected-trade review, and visual system
route composition, worker patch integration, and verified repairs only
review completed source and visible evidence without private checks

rules: Commit the product brief and each frozen contract before the corresponding model sees it.
Use a new isolated worktree and non-persistent session for every model stage.
Do not expose benchmark/private, earlier model transcripts, or another worker's hidden reasoning.
Workers may read shared contracts but may change only their owned files.
Preserve failed runs, partial patches, denied tools, provider errors, and timeouts.
Do not rerun a failed worker inside this block.
Do not make an OpenRouter call until a fresh dollar ceiling is explicitly approved.
Do not increase provider limits, enable Anthropic usage credits, push, deploy, or use real trade data.
Do not compare token totals across adapters unless their definitions match.
Do not claim production, booking, settlement, pricing, or regulatory readiness.
